candidates.source_title: The Mathematician Who Tried to Predict His Own Future #history
candidates.source_description:
In 1754, mathematician Abraham de Moivre reportedly noticed he was sleeping 15 minutes longer each night. According to the famous story, he used that pattern to calculate his own final day: November 27, 1754—the date he actually passed away, aged 87. A pioneer of probability theory, de Moivre left behind a remarkable mathematical legacy, though this prediction should be presented as a historical anecdote rather than a proven feat.
